title: Chapter 606
paragraphs: Chapter 606
Episode 156. Purification of Chaos (10)
'How many times have I fainted now?'
As soon as he opened his eyes, Jin could see his brothers looking down at him with worried faces, as always.
"You're awake, Brother Jin."
"I'm not sure how many times I've heard that. I'm getting tired of losing consciousness. How long has it passed this time?"
"Two days."
"Huh."
A sense of defeat, or anger.
These emotions were making Jin's chest hot like a furnace.
Gulp, gulp! Despite gulping down the cold water Nata offered, the heat didn't seem to fade. The more he thought, the hotter he felt, and Chaos seemed so cunning he felt like going mad.
"What the hell happened inside? It wasn't even 1 or 2 minutes after you went in, and you came back so beaten up. Not anyone else, but Brother Jin...."
"Let's talk first."
"When I went in, it was his subspace, he was bigger, he was right in front of me, and he broke me in one hit. He even read all my thoughts, just like I did outside."
There wasn't much to explain at length. The match was indeed decided in one strike.

"He also said that spirit energy isn't much of a threat in there. That damned guy, he could talk. He even mocked me asking how the taste of his powerful front kick was... This is the first time I've been so utterly defeated."
"Is it really the first time?"
Vahn spoke as he sat down next to the bed where Jin was lying.
Unlike the serious Jin and the other brothers, Vahn seemed to find this situation amusing, wearing a slight smile.

"When Brother Jin first came here, most of the brothers thought you were an immature genius. You probably hadn't experienced much defeat outside, and therefore, they guessed your mentality would be weak."
"Brother Tusin."
"But in fact, Brother Jin was someone who was familiar with defeat. When you first came to Lafralosa, you were only beaten by the other brothers until you left."
"That's true."
"So, don't put special meaning into this defeat."
Jin felt a sudden sense of clarity.
Just as Vahn said, he had already experienced numerous defeats. He had gone through countless instances of greater despair and injustice than having his power stolen by Chaos.
Especially compared to the period before regression, when he was cursed, the current situation was 'somewhat manageable'.
"Brother Jin."
"Speak, Brother Tusin."
"Allow me to ask one thing. Do you still want to face him with your own strength, without the help of me and the brothers?"
"Yes, I do."
"Then, training starts now."
Vahn concluded succinctly.
"You have three years, Jin. During that time, I and the other brothers will personally train you so that you can defeat him. And whenever you reach a certain point, you will rematch him."
Unlike Jin, the Demon Kings did not experience the chaos in the void. They could only infer his power based on Jin's explanation, and Jin himself could not know precisely due to the significant gap.
One thing was certain, at the present, he was at a level that could easily annihilate Jin.
Training for a day or two wouldn't solve the problem, meaning Jin had to face the void and prepare for death each time.
"Whether you were lucky or there was another reason, you made it back alive. Even if you lose the next fight, just survive and escape again."
Of course, it was dangerous, but the Demon Kings remembered what Vahn had said.
"Well, I am worried about Jin, but as Brother Tusin said, training inherently carries the risk of death..."
"If Jin wants to fight alone, that's the only answer, really."
Jin and the Demon Kings quickly agreed with Vahn's opinion.
"In addition, other brothers will also train together with Jin."
"Sister Vahn, when should I plan for the next rematch?"
"One month from now."
The time was woefully inadequate to close the gap. Even the Demon Kings expressed doubts about the quick turnaround, but Vahn was firm.

"Fight again in a month and gather more information about him. Reconnaissance, understanding, combat, escape. It's going to be a long and dangerous battle that only Jin can do. Everyone, move to the second training ground."
That one month became the most hellish time in Jin's life.
And it was merely the 'beginning'.
'I never thought I would hope for the day not to come due to the agony of training...'
As he vomited bile, goosebumps ran all over his body.
The Demon Kings' training was rough, incomparable to that of humans. However, the standard of 'Tusin' was even higher.
The other Demon Kings also had vacant eyes, nearly on the verge of death. However, they quickly recovered after a few hours of rest, whereas Jin continued training, completely drained.
Vahn mercilessly informed Jin, who was in such a state, that the scheduled rematch date was nearing.
"Jin, take a day off and enter the gate tomorrow. So, today's training is over."
Jin misunderstood her words as 'rest by entering the gate.'

So, he stumbled out of the second training ground, heading towards the central training ground (Vahn naturally assumed Jin was heading to his room to rest), trying to enter the gate, but was stopped by Tantel and Shaku, who were on guard. If it weren't for the two of them, he would have directly confronted the chaos again.
"Jin, you're going to rest by entering the gate? Brother Tusin couldn't have said that!"
"Training... part of training..."
"Wait, I'll check. Oh, he passed out."
"Ugh, let's move him to his room."
When he opened his eyes again, it was a familiar ceiling.
'Brother Tusin told me to rest in the room...! No, something's strange. Did I mishear?'
Tusin Vahn chuckled at the sight of Jin flustered as soon as he regained consciousness. Then, meeting Jin's eyes, he quickly straightened his face and said,
"Let's go, it's the second battle."
As always, all the brothers were waiting in front of the door. Given the hellish training that had been going on until just a moment ago, the Ming royal family had the air of well-sharpened swords.
Jin had only slept for a day. Of course, the fatigue didn't go away, and his whole body felt heavy as if soaked in water.
Jin had to fight the second battle in that state.
'At this point, it seems like Brother Tusin is determined to kill me.'
If it weren't for their blind faith in their brothers, especially Tusin Vahn, Jin would have screamed that this was insane.
"I'll be back."
"Good luck."
"Come back alive, Brother Jin!"
When he entered the room, it was the same as last time. An unexpected darkness spread out, and the bastard's voice came.
[Oh, you're here?]
As soon as he faced the chaos, the accumulated fatigue seemed to turn into anger all at once. It was time to see the results of the hellish training...
Jin came out of the room again exactly three minutes later.
[Anyway, you brat. So when are you going to fight a real fight? Yawning, I'm yawning!]
The chaos was still mocking Jin until the crack made by the Holy Sword closed.
"Brother Jin is back alive!"
"Brother Otu King, treatment!"
The Ming royal family were in a fuss, but Vahn just calmly said,
"Three minutes, much better than last time."
"But Brother Tusin, Brother Jin's injury is more severe this time. It seems like he was lucky to escape this time, but we should postpone the third battle...!"
"No, the third battle will also proceed as scheduled in a month. Brother Otu King, do whatever it takes to make sure Brother Jin can train from tonight."
From Jin's perspective, it felt like there were two devils. The chaos beyond the door, and Tusin Vahn.
However, Jin was feeling a strange emotion along with his anger.
'Somehow Sister Vahn... seems to be certain that I won't die. Is it a delusion?'
He didn't have time to think deeply. As expected, Boras 'made Jin movable' by healing him from the night, and the hellish training resumed for a month straight.
"I'll be back..."
[The idiot is here again. You were lucky to escape last time, weren't you? Die today!]
He returned alive.
"2 minutes and 34 seconds. It's actually less than last time!"

"But the injuries have decreased as well. It seems like Brother Tusin's decision to only focus on escape training for the last two months is starting to pay off. Brother Jin, the fight time has shortened because you escaped at the right time, right?"
A similar pattern continued in the fourth battle that unfolded another month later.
Every time, Jin was easily defeated to the point of emptiness, and chaos seemed to just barely miss Jin.
"3 minutes 57 seconds!"
[Cackle, keep trying for a hundred days!]
"4 minutes 12 seconds!"
[No, no. So you can't even scratch a single one of my scales.]
"12 minutes 36 seconds! Plus, this time Brother Jin came back with only one broken arm!"
"Just? Just? Want to try breaking once, brother?"
[You're getting pretty good at dodging my strong front paw swing, aren't you? But what to do, I haven't even shown you my super-strong tail swing yet.]
"18 minutes 27 seconds...!"
[Tsk, you run away well again...! Next time, I'll definitely send you to the other world!]
The day he recorded 18 minutes and 27 seconds was, before he knew it, a year later.
By that time, Jin was facing chaos with some mental leeway. It was still very small, but hope was starting to show.
"Every time you miss me. Having watched you quietly for the past year, you're all talk. See you in a month, wait with your neck out. Keep my energy well."
[I don't want to, I don't want to! Ebebebebek!]
Jin unknowingly burst into a small laugh for the first time. It was the first time in the past year.
"Oh, Brother Jin has finally returned without major injuries! Any effective hits?"
"Not yet. We did manage to bruise it a few times, but we couldn't inflict any major damage."
"That's nothing, Brother Jin. You're great!"
That day, the Ming royal family were almost in a festival mood when they saw Jin return without injury.
Some brothers even wiped their eyes recalling the terrible training process Jin had gone through.
Vahn also ruffled Jin's hair for the first time, praising him.
"Well done, Brother Jin. In the next fight, you will be able to truly threaten it."
"I think so too, Brother Tusin. I've regained more power from it, and I think the ultimate technique of the Holy Sword that I'm about to master will soon reach its peak..."
Jin, who answered like that, was looking at the emptiness beyond the door.
Suddenly, he was curious about what chaos would be doing there when he was not present.
